text:
A year ago I started this company with a pitch deck, way too much coffee, and more confidence than I'd earned.

Year one in numbers: $180k in revenue, a team of 4, 2 failed pivots, and 17 paying customers by month 11.

The pivots are what I keep coming back to. Both times I was convinced we'd found it, and both times the market said no. They felt like failures when they happened. Now I'd call them the most expensive lessons we paid for all year, and the most useful. Each one showed us something customers didn't need, and once we'd ruled those things out, it got easier to see what they actually wanted.

A few other things I learned:

Small teams move fast when everyone owns the result. I couldn't have asked for a better 3 people to build this with.

Revenue is the most honest feedback you'll get. Compliments cost nothing. Paying for something is a real commitment.

Getting to 17 paying customers in month 11 meant more to me than any metric I could put on a slide. Those were real people choosing us.

Year one humbled me. In year two we build on what's working.

To everyone who believed in us early: thank you. We're just getting started.
